newsitem.title: UK: Lawyer calls UK match-fixing trial witness a liar.
newsitem.headline: Lawyer calls UK match-fixing trial witness a liar.

text.p: The chief witness against Bruce Grobbelaar in Britain's football match-fixing case admitted he had wanted to crush the former Liverpool goalkeeper.

Grobbelaar's lawyer Rodney Klevan portrayed Chris Vincent in a two-hour session on Tuesday as a parasite who was happy to live off the footballer's money but who turned on him when he stopped investing in a safari company the two were running.
"You've been telling lies to us, Mr Vincent, as we shall see tomorrow," Klevan told the court in Winchester, southwest England.
Vincent admitted in cross-examination he wanted to make as much money as he could from the case while crushing Grobbelaar, who he blamed for the collapse of the safari company.

Grobbelaar is accused of fixing matches with the help of former striker John Fashanu and Malaysian businessmen Heng Suan Lim. A fourth man on trial is former Wimbledon goalkeeper Hans Segers, accused with Lim and Fashanu of taking part in a separate bid to fix matches. All four pleaded not guilty.
Vincent covertly filmed Grobbelaar as he allegedly admitted rigging games for a Far Eastern betting syndicate.

On one tape, the keeper is seen taking an envelope which the prosecution claims contains 2,000 pounds ($3,322) from Vincent as payment from what he is alleged to have believed was another betting group. But the syndicate had been dreamed up to trap Grobbelaar.
"Therefore, if you could kill two birds with one stone, you would gain financially and destroy Grobbelaar?" asked Klevan.
"Correct, sir," answered Vincent, 37, who stayed calm during the interrogation.

Vincent admitted that since 1984 he had been director of four companies in southern Africa and Britain, all of which had failed. He invested none of his own money in the safari company while Grobbelaar put in 65,000 pounds.
"Are you proud of your commercial record?" asked Klevan.
"I would say I have been subject to an incredible amount of bad luck," Vincent replied to laughter in the court.
Vincent said he did not go to the police because at the time he did not know that match-rigging was banned.
"Are you saying that a man of your age and experience of the world didn't know that the fixing of matches could be illegal?" Klevan asked in disbelief.
"No, but it could be morally wrong," answered Vincent.
The prosecution says Grobbelaar tried to rig four games for a Far Eastern syndicate while playing for Liverpool and Southampton.
Vincent says he was with Grobbelaar when the player received 40,000 pounds in late 1993 for throwing an away match against Newcastle when still playing for Liverpool. ($1=.6021 Pound)
